subject.title: Enhancement: Developer experience quick wins from code analysis

question: Should the remaining work stay in this umbrella, and which operator-visible surface should successful non-tool skill prompt rewrites use?
rationale: The missing source paths are clear, but status performance boundaries and prompt-rewrite warning UX are product choices rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Split focused follow-ups
options.body: Track status registry diagnostics separately from prompt-rewrite diagnostics, decide the warning surface first, and keep each implementation bounded with targeted tests.

options.title: Keep the umbrella
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker for both remaining quick wins, accepting that implementation spans status, skills, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to status diagnostics
options.body: Treat the shipped skills check and docs as enough for skill invocation debugging and keep only the status registry diagnostics request.

recommendation.title: Split focused follow-ups
recommendation.body: Track status registry diagnostics separately from prompt-rewrite diagnostics, decide the warning surface first, and keep each implementation bounded with targeted tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the prior keep-open review and is tied by current source history to all affected surfaces.
